title: Embedding Eval: Sampling Protocol for Low-Resource Languages
body:
Purpose:
This doc defines a repeatable sampling and probe protocol for embedding evaluation focused on low-resource languages (LRLs). Goal is to produce small, high-signal eval sets that uncover retrieval and clustering regressions when we onboard new models or quantization profiles. Keep it lean: targeting 1k-5k total items per language family per smoke suite.

Scope:
- Languages: small-script and low-resource languages (examples: Amharic, Yoruba, Khmer, Lao, Nepali, Pashto).
- Use cases: semantic search (recall@k, MRR), clustering sanity (purity, silhouette), multilingual neighborhood consistency.
- Not covered: full scale production embedsets (these live in curated corpora). This is a fast probe suite for onboarding.

High-level approach:
1) Anchor pairs: build bilingual anchor pairs by pulling high-quality parallel segments (2–3 sentence spans) where available (Wikimedia, JW300, OPUS). When parallel data absent, generate anchors with professional translations or stable MT + post-edit where budget allows. Anchors are used for cross-lingual recall tests and UMAP anchor checks.
2) Monolingual diversity sampling: sample documents across 4 axes: domain (news, wiki, community forums, product docs), length (short <50 char, medium 50–300, long >300), script (native vs latin-translit), register (formal vs informal). Aim for 250–500 examples per axis cell where possible.
3) Query-document pairing: for semantic search probes, create realistic query sets by extracting question-like sentences and manual query rewriting to emulate user intent. Each query should have 3 gold positives (exact, related, paraphrase) and several negatives drawn from near-neighbors by tf-idf to stress model.
4) Translation augmentation: where native content is scarce, translate a subset of high-quality English seed items into target LRLs using two MT engines and keep items where engines agree (filter by BLEU/chrF thresholds). Flag synthetic vs natural in annotations.

Sampling protocol details:
- Minimum per-language sample: 1,000 documents (500 docs + 500 queries) for a smoke pass; full probe: 3,000+ items.
- Stratification: ensure at least 20% short-form content, 30% user-generated style, 10% domain-specific (legal/medical where allowed).
- Script balance: include both native script and latinized versions where transliteration is common to mimic real inputs.
- Negative mining: for each query, sample 10 hard negatives from corpus nearest-neighbors (embedding baseline) and 10 random negatives.

Labeling and annotation guidance:
- Label types: exact_match, semantic_match, related, not_relevant. Provide examples per language; for synthetic items add "synthetic" tag.
- Annotation instructions: emphasize paraphrase vs related distinction; training hit-rate should be >= 85% on golden examples before annotators proceed.
- QA: implement a 5% blind re-labeling by a second annotator, compute Cohen's kappa; target >= 0.7 for acceptance.

Metrics to compute:
- Retrieval: recall@1/5/10, MRR, MAP (where multiple positives exist).
- Ranking robustness: delta-recall vs baseline, inversion rate (pairs that flip order relative to baseline).
- Clustering: pairwise purity, silhouette score on common-language clusters, neighbor overlap (top-10 reciprocal neighbors).
- Multilingual consistency: anchor recall (do translation anchors map to same neighborhood), cosine drift between language variants, bilingual retrieval AUC.
- Confidence: bootstrap 1k resamples to get 95% CI on recall@k.

Smoke checks and visualization:
- UMAP plot per-language with color by domain and by synthetic/natural tag. Look for language islands and anchor alignment.
- Neighbor tables for 50 random queries in each language (show top-10 neighbors and mark golds).
- Token-length vs similarity scatter to catch truncation artifacts.
- Embedding norm distribution per language and per model variant.

Regression thresholds and alerting:
- Set soft thresholds: degrade if recall@10 drops >4% absolute vs baseline, or anchor recall drops >6%.
- Hard fail: if MRR drops >10% or silhouette collapses by >0.2.
- Integrate with CI: automated eval runs on PRs that change tokenization, quantization, or model family; post results to PR and to monitoring dashboard.

Operational notes (practicalities):
- Storage: eval sets kept in /datasets/embed-evals/lrl/<lang>/ with metadata JSON including provenance and synthetic flag.
- Repro: include seed RNG and script versions; record MT engine versions and post-edit notes.
- Budgeting: translation/post-edit budget should prioritize anchor creation and domain-specific items.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which LRLs get priority in Q1? (Stakeholders: Solutions Eng, Growth)
- How to price post-edit for anchors — propose per-anchor cap $25.
- Can SRE add a tiny GPU job to precompute baseline neighbors for negative mining? Ticket: JIRA-ENG-INF-2109 (dependency).
- Decide whether to include ASR-derived transcripts for spoken-domain coverage.

Checklist before onboarding a new model:
- [ ] Generate language-specific corpus sample and run script to stratify by domain/length
- [ ] Create anchors (parallel or translated) and flag synthetic items
- [ ] Produce queries + gold positives, run negative mining against baseline
- [ ] Send for annotation and pass QA kappa threshold
- [ ] Run full eval suite, bootstrap CIs, produce visualizations
- [ ] Post results to Confluence and link PR for model change

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the smoke set intentionally small so CI runs fast (~15-20 minutes). Full run can be nightly.
- For Khmer/Lao we may need native script tokenization tweaks; check tokenization corner cases with runtime team.
- Consider adding a "typing noise" augmentation to simulate user input with diacritics removed.

References and provenance:
- corpora: OPUS, CC-100 derived splits, Wikipedia dumps
- tooling: eval repo https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-eval, labeling UI: internal-labeler v2
- related tickets: JIRA-ENG-ML-4321 (embed onboarding backlog), JIRA-ENG-INF-2109 (precompute neighbors)

End of doc. Feedback welcome — this is a working protocol, expect iterations after first few language passes.
